diseases.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves that turn dark brown to black with yellow halos. Severely affected leaves may yellow and drop. Fruit develops raised, brown, scab-like spots.
diseases.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides at first sign of disease. Remove and destroy infected plant debris. Avoid overhead watering to reduce leaf wetness. Use bactericidal sprays containing copper hydroxide every 7-10 days during favorable conditions.
diseases.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds. Practice crop rotation with non-host crops for 2-3 years. Avoid working in fields when plants are wet. Maintain proper plant spacing for air circulation. Disinfect tools between plants.
diseases.favorable_conditions: Warm temperatures (24-30°C) with high humidity or frequent rain. Splashing water spreads the bacteria.

diseases.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Leaves appear green, firm, and free from spots or discoloration.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed. Continue regular care.
diseases.prevention: Maintain consistent watering schedule. Ensure adequate sunlight (6-8 hours daily). Use balanced fertilizer every 2-3 weeks. Monitor regularly for early signs of disease or pests. Keep area weed-free.
diseases.favorable_conditions: Plant appears to be growing in suitable conditions. Continue best practices.

diseases.symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings (target-like pattern) on older leaves first. Yellow halos surround the spots. Leaves may turn yellow and drop. Tubers can develop dark, sunken spots.
diseases.treatment: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb at first symptoms. Repeat applications every 7-10 days during favorable conditions. Remove and destroy infected plant debris. Improve air circulation by proper spacing.
diseases.prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-Solanaceae crops. Use disease-resistant varieties when available. Maintain proper plant nutrition, especially potassium. Avoid overhead irrigation. Mulch to reduce soil splash.
diseases.favorable_conditions: Warm temperatures (24-29°C) with alternating wet and dry periods. Plant stress from drought or poor nutrition increases susceptibility.

diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked, pale green spots on leaves that rapidly turn dark brown or black. White fuzzy growth appears on undersides of leaves in humid conditions. Stems may develop brown to black lesions. Tubers show firm, brown, granular rot.
diseases.treatment: URGENT: Apply systemic fungicides like metalaxyl or cymoxanil immediately. Remove and destroy infected plants — do not compost. Increase fungicide application frequency to every 5-7 days during outbreak. Consider early harvest if disease is severe.
diseases.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed potatoes. Plant resistant varieties. Avoid overhead irrigation. Destroy volunteer potato plants and cull piles. Apply preventive fungicides before disease appears in high-risk weather.
diseases.favorable_conditions: Cool, wet weather (15-20°C) with high humidity. Disease can spread rapidly during cool nights and warm days. Historic cause of the Irish Potato Famine.

diseases.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Leaves appear green, vigorous, and free from spots, lesions, or discoloration.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed. Continue regular care.
diseases.prevention: Hill soil around plants to prevent tuber greening. Maintain consistent moisture. Apply balanced fertilizer with adequate potassium. Monitor for pests like Colorado potato beetle. Practice crop rotation.
diseases.favorable_conditions: Plant appears to be in good health. Continue current management practices.

diseases.symptoms: Small dark brown to black water-soaked spots on leaves, often with yellow halos. Spots may merge causing large dead areas. Fruit develops raised, scab-like brown spots. Affected leaves may yellow and drop, exposing fruit to sunscald.
diseases.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides at first symptoms, repeated every 7-10 days. Combine with mancozeb for better efficacy. Remove infected plant debris. Avoid overhead irrigation and working with wet plants.
diseases.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds and transplants. Practice 2-3 year crop rotation. Avoid working in wet fields. Disinfect tools and stakes. Use resistant varieties where available. Mulch to prevent soil splash.
diseases.favorable_conditions: Warm, humid weather (24-30°C) with frequent rain. Splashing water spreads bacteria. Plant injury from wind, insects, or handling provides entry points.

diseases.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked spots on leaves that rapidly turn brown or black. White, fuzzy mold appears on leaf undersides in humid conditions. Stems develop dark, water-soaked lesions. Green fruits develop firm, brown, greasy-looking spots.
diseases.treatment: URGENT: Apply protective fungicides (chlorothalonil, mancozeb) preventively in high-risk weather. Use systemic fungicides (metalaxyl, cymoxanil) at first signs. Remove infected plants immediately — destroy, do not compost. Consider crop loss if disease is widespread.
diseases.prevention: Plant resistant varieties when available. Provide good air circulation with proper spacing and staking. Avoid overhead watering. Apply preventive fungicides during humid weather. Remove volunteer tomatoes and potatoes that harbor disease.
diseases.favorable_conditions: Cool, wet weather (15-22°C) with extended leaf wetness. High humidity above 75%. Spreads rapidly during cool nights and overcast days. Can destroy crops in 7-10 days under favorable conditions.

diseases.symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces. Olive-green to gray-brown velvety mold develops on the undersides, directly beneath the spots. Affected leaves curl, wither, and drop. Stems and fruit are rarely affected.
diseases.treatment: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or copper compounds. Spray particularly on leaf undersides. Improve air circulation by removing lower leaves and increasing plant spacing. Reduce humidity in greenhouses through ventilation.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant varieties (Cf-genes resistant). Ensure good air circulation through proper pruning and spacing. Reduce humidity, especially in greenhouses. Water at soil level, not on foliage. Stake plants to keep foliage off the ground.
diseases.favorable_conditions: High humidity (above 85%) with moderate temperatures (22-25°C). Common in greenhouses and high tunnels. Less problematic in open field conditions with good air movement.

diseases.symptoms: Tiny yellow or white speckles (stippling) on upper leaf surfaces, gradually turning leaves bronzed or pale. Fine webbing visible on leaf undersides and between leaves in severe infestations. Mites barely visible to naked eye. Leaves may dry out and drop.
diseases.treatment: Spray water forcefully on leaf undersides to dislodge mites. Apply insecticidal soap or horticultural oil thoroughly to undersides of leaves. Use specific miticides (abamectin, bifenazate) for severe infestations. Beneficial predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis) provide biological control.
diseases.prevention: Maintain adequate soil moisture — drought-stressed plants are more susceptible. Encourage beneficial predators by avoiding broad-spectrum insecticides. Remove weeds that harbor mites. Regularly inspect leaf undersides, especially during hot, dry weather.
diseases.favorable_conditions: Hot, dry conditions (above 27°C with low humidity). Mites reproduce rapidly in these conditions — a generation can complete in 5-7 days. Dusty conditions favor mites.

diseases.symptoms: Small dark spots that enlarge to form characteristic 'target' patterns with concentric rings — similar to early blight but typically darker and without yellow halos. Leaf, stem, and fruit can all be affected. Fruit spots are dark, sunken, and may have concentric rings.
diseases.treatment: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or azoxystrobin. Begin applications at first sign of disease and repeat every 7-10 days. Remove and destroy infected plant debris. Improve air circulation.
diseases.prevention: Practice crop rotation with non-host crops. Use drip irrigation instead of overhead watering. Stake plants and prune lower leaves to improve airflow. Maintain proper plant nutrition. Apply preventive fungicides in humid weather.
diseases.favorable_conditions: Warm, humid conditions (24-28°C with high humidity or leaf wetness). Disease worsens with overhead irrigation and dense plantings.

diseases.symptoms: Severe yellowing and upward curling of leaf margins. Leaves become smaller and crumpled. Plant growth is severely stunted. Flowers drop without setting fruit. Existing fruit may ripen unevenly or remain small. Bushy appearance with shortened internodes.
diseases.treatment: No cure exists once plants are infected — remove and destroy infected plants immediately to prevent spread. Control whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) vector with insecticidal soap, neem oil, or systemic insecticides. Use yellow sticky traps to monitor whitefly populations.
diseases.prevention: Plant resistant or tolerant varieties (look for 'TY' designation). Cover seedlings with fine mesh to exclude whiteflies. Use reflective mulches to repel whiteflies. Control weeds that harbor whiteflies. Remove infected plants promptly. Plant during cooler seasons when whitefly populations are lower.
diseases.favorable_conditions: Hot, dry weather favors whitefly populations. Virus is transmitted by whiteflies in 15-30 minutes of feeding. Once transmitted, plants show symptoms in 2-3 weeks. Major problem in tropical and subtropical regions including most of India.

diseases.pathogen: Tomato Mosaic Virus (ToMV) / Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV)
diseases.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green pattern (mosaic) on leaves. Leaves may be malformed, narrow, or fern-like. Plants may be stunted. Fruit can show yellow or brown internal discoloration and uneven ripening. Symptoms vary based on virus strain and tomato variety.
diseases.treatment: No cure available — remove and destroy infected plants immediately. Disinfect tools, hands, and surfaces with 10% bleach solution or milk after handling infected plants. Smokers should wash hands thoroughly with soap before handling plants — tobacco can carry TMV.
diseases.prevention: Use certified virus-free seeds and resistant varieties. Wash hands and disinfect tools between plants. Avoid smoking or handling tobacco near tomatoes. Control aphids that can spread the virus. Remove weeds that may harbor the virus.
diseases.favorable_conditions: Virus spreads through mechanical contact — hands, tools, clothing, and contaminated water. Can survive in plant debris and soil for months. Stable virus that can withstand drying and brief exposure to heat.

diseases.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Leaves appear green, firm, and free from spots, mottling, or distortion.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed. Continue regular care.
diseases.prevention: Maintain consistent watering (1-2 inches per week, deep watering preferred). Provide support with stakes or cages. Mulch to retain moisture and prevent soil splash. Apply balanced fertilizer with calcium to prevent blossom end rot. Regular inspection for early disease detection.
diseases.favorable_conditions: Plant appears to be growing well. Maintain optimal conditions: 21-29°C daytime, 16-20°C nighttime, full sun, well-draining soil with pH 6.0-6.8.
